summary: Some attractions, restaurants and traditional inns ask guests to remove their shoes; shoe racks and slippers are usually provided, so watch for signs and follow what others do.
Tipping is not customary and can confuse staff; a thank-you in Japanese and a smile are the usual way to show appreciation.
On trains and buses, passengers commonly keep their voices down, avoid phone calls and use headphones for music or videos.
At onsen and public baths, bathers wash and rinse before getting into the shared bath, and swimwear is not worn in the water.
Washoku, the traditional food culture of the Japanese, especially as practiced around New Year, was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013.
